review_rounds.harness_note: Roles were told v0.31.2 had just shipped and to judge 0.32.0 against the current tree rather than the tree it was drafted against, with a list of what changed. implementer was given five load-bearing claims to verify against real code; tester was given the existing test files; ax-economist was told 0.31.2 enlarged the per-role prompt cost this feature lets a project decline.

Roles were told the spec was rewritten rather than patched (treat as a new document), given the old->new section renumbering, and each asked to re-examine the change their own round-1 high drove: architect on whether deleting the old trim_candidate section leaves §1's cited complaint unanswered, ax-economist on whether §1.1's arithmetic overstates the saving, implementer on five load-bearing code claims, tester on the 16 test items.

Roles were asked to re-derive the changes their own round-2 highs drove, and two were asked pointed questions about whether my fix opened a new door: architect on whether the --no-state carve-out makes the guard optional in practice, ax-economist on whether §2.6's doubled length is the feature's complexity or the tree's.

Two changes since round 3: §2.6's refusal was cut to a warning, and the spec was compressed 50% (3386 -> 1677 words) by removing rationale prose while keeping every requirement. Roles were told the removal was deliberate and instructed NOT to report 'the spec no longer explains why' — only lost requirements. regression was told the compression is the change most likely to have broken something.
